facts: Pulicherla Nagaraju @ Nagaraja Reddy v State of Andhra Pradesh
The prosecution case, in brief, is as under : P. Narasimha Reddy (PW-2) and P. Govinda Reddy (Accused No.1) are brothers.
Both families were residents of Bangareddipalli Diguva Indlu, a hamlet falling under the Gangadhara Nellore Panchayat in Chittoor District.
Narasimha Reddy, after his marriage, having differences with his parents had shifted to his father-in-law's place and then to Madras.
Govinda Reddy was in possession and enjoyment of the family properties.
On 24.4.1999, Narasimha Reddy (PW-2) brought some plastic pipes to his house in a hired tractor.
On 25.4.1999 at about 6 p.m., Govinda Reddy with his wife (A2) and sons (A3 and two juveniles) removed a part of the fence surrounding Narasimha Reddy's property.
Within about half an hour of the second incident, Purushotham Reddy (first son of Narasimha Reddy) returned home.
Purushotham Reddy, followed by his father (PW-2) and brother (PW-1), went towards the house of Govinda Reddy to question them about their high-handed acts.
Govinda Reddy was armed with a stick with nails, Ranamma was armed with stout stick, Nagaraja was armed with a Barisa.
issues: Whether the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 could be relied upon?
Whether the rejection of the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 by the trial court was justified?
Whether the charge u/s. 302 was proved against A-3 and that the charge u/s. 302 read with s. 34 IPC was not proved against A1 and A2.
petitioner_arguments: The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 could be relied upon.
The rejection of the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 by the trial court was unjustified and perverse.
The charge u/s. 302 was proved against A-3 and that the charge u/s. 302 read with s. 34 IPC was not proved against A1 and A2.
respondent_arguments: The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 could not be relied upon as they were close relatives of the deceased, having previous enmity and grudge against the accused and who were interested in falsely implicating the accused.
The rejection of the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 by the trial court was justified.
The charge u/s. 302 read with s. 34 IPC was proved against A1 and A2.
court_reasoning: The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2, who were eye-witnesses, could not be rejected merely on the ground that they were interested or partisan, as their evidence was otherwise found to be credible.

The second incident which occurred at about 6.00 to 7.00 P.M. wherein PW-1 and PW-2 were attacked and injured and the third incident within about half an hour thereof when Purushotham Reddy was killed should be considered as having occurred during the course of the same transaction in the sense that the latter incident was a continuation and consequence of the earlier incident.

Nothing was elicited in the cross-examination of PW-1 and PW-2 to disbelieve their evidence about the incidents, in particular the manner in which they were attacked and injured by accused 1 and 3 and the manner in which Purushottam Reddy was killed by Nagaraja Reddy (A-3).
Though the incident took place at 7.30 P.M. and there were no light, the evidence of PWs.1 and 2 that could see the accused clearly in the moonlight ought to be accepted.
The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 established that A-1 to A3 caught the deceased and A-3 stabbed him near the throat with MO1 Barisa (long dagger).
The medical evidence corroborated that the injury was caused of a weapon like MO1.
holding: The charge u/s. 302 was proved against A-3 and that the charge u/s. 302 read with s. 34 IPC was not proved against A1 and A2.
The judgment of the trial court was set aside and the appeal was allowed.
